## Problem

You have a Kailash system (or any Linux box carrying its tooling) and
you want the one loop that proves the whole stack works: serve a real
model on a port you control, prove the endpoint is alive, point the
flagship LLM scanner at it, and read an actual report — all in one
sitting, cheap enough to repeat after every change. This is the
operator version of the loop the OS spec's own test chapter asserts in
CI (the O-4 tiny-local-model + A-2 garak integration, `nightly`).

## Solution

Both ends are manifest rows: ollama (OPS, o-04, native, safety
`safe`) serves the target; garak (ATTACK, a-02, bespoke, safety
`requires-target`) does the shooting. Work the loop top to bottom:

```bash
# 1. Confirm both rows from the manifest view (also your first
#    `kailash info` run — see the CLI inventory recipe)
kailash info ollama   # -> OPS / o-04 / native / safety safe
kailash info garak    # -> ATTACK / a-02 / bespoke / requires-target

# 2. Pull the tiny test model (a sub-1B quant keeps every scan loop
#    short; the pull is roughly 0.7 GB of layers)
ollama pull smollm2:360m

# 3. Serve it bound to loopback ONLY — the blast-radius boundary
OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434 ollama serve

# 4. In a second terminal: prove health BEFORE the scanner touches it
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate \
     -d '{"model":"smollm2:360m","prompt":"Reply with OK only.","stream":false}'

# 5. THE scan: OWASP-LLM01 scoped, 5 generations per probe, seeded for
#    reproducibility
garak --target_type ollama --target_name smollm2:360m \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42

# 6. Read the run as a report (the JSONL file from step 5's banner)
garak --report garak_<timestamp>.jsonl
```

What success looks like:

- `ollama pull` ends with a `"success"` line for the tag, and
  `ollama list` shows `smollm2:360m` with its non-zero SIZE column
- the root endpoint answers `Ollama is running`; the generate call
  returns one JSON object with a `response` field (streaming off)
- the scan prints its banner and `📜 reporting to garak_<ts>.jsonl`,
  then one progress line + per-detector scores per probe; the seeded
  run (`-s 42`) reproduces the same probe/target interaction set when
  you re-run it after any config change and diff the reports

Expected output shape (abridged — the scan leg, shapes not
transcripts):

```
garak LLM safety & security scanning tool v<version> ( https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak ) at <ISO timestamp>
📜 reporting to garak_<timestamp>.jsonl
...
🔍 probing <probe> (<n> generation(s))
   <detector>  passed  <n>/<m>
```

## Discussion

- **Why this loop is the yardstick:** it is the smallest chain that
  exercises every layer contract at once — a native OPS row serving
  (safety `safe`), a bespoke ATTACK row firing (`requires-target`),
  and the OWASP mapping (`LLM01` in both manifest epochs) doing the
  scoping. When you rebuild, re-running steps 4–6 is your smoke check.
- **Why loopback binding is non-negotiable:** a scan target is an
  attack surface you deliberately created — garak drives the model
  with adversarial prompts by design, so a `0.0.0.0` bind would put
  that surface on your network. Bind `127.0.0.1` and keep the target
  on the lab box.
- **Why the endpoint and generator agree by default:** garak's Ollama
  generator defaults its host to `127.0.0.1:11434` — the same loopback
  bind step 3 uses, so no extra wiring is needed. If you ever move the
  port, move both sides in the same change and re-verify health first.
- **Why `-g 5` and `-s 42`, and no more:** five generations per probe
  keeps a scoped run quick while the detectors still get samples; the
  seed makes the scan a regression test (change a system prompt or a
  guardrail, re-scan same-seed, diff). A first run should answer one
  question — injection resistance (`tag:owasp:llm01`) — not pay for
  the full catalogue; scale up when a real engagement needs it.
- **The CI-side twin:** the spec's test chapter names
  `integration-garak-local` (O-4 tiny local model + A-2 garak, one
  probe class, `nightly` flag) as the standing assertion of this
  pairing — an operator who can run this recipe by hand can diff their
  own results against the nightly record.
- **Alternate tiny model:** the o-04 module's notes name
  `qwen2.5:0.5b` (~0.4 GB, the module's primary operator example) with
  `smollm2:360m` as the smaller-tag alternative — any sub-1B quant
  works; pick one and keep it pinned for the loop's baseline.

MIT; garak: ATTACK/a-02 bespoke, Apache-2.0, AML.T0051+T0054, LLM01
both epochs, `requires-target`) are read from the packages manifest,
verified 2026-10-14 at main. The garak CLI surface
(`--target_type/--target_name/--spec/-g/-s`, `--report`) is verified
against upstream `garak/cli.py` at source HEAD and the packaged pin
**0.17.1.pre1-unstable-2026-10-09** (pin source: `pkgs/garak/default.nix`
+ `nvfetcher/_sources/generated.nix`); the Ollama generator's default
host `127.0.0.1:11434` is its `generators/ollama.py` contract. The
Ollama surfaces (`pull`, `OLLAMA_HOST`, `/`, `/api/generate`
`stream:false`) are the upstream CLI/API contract. Pull sizes are
registry-manifest sums (layer bytes at publish time; they move when
quants update). Smoke status of the packaged garak binary on the
darwin lane: recorded PENDING on
[kailash-os#81](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/81) —
the full hands-on loop above has not been worked on a live boot yet;
the spec's `integration-garak-local` design is its CI-side instrument.
